Nine methods in `lib/response.js` and one helper in `lib/router/index.js` call `res.set`. I searched `lib/` for every `.set(` and `.header(` call and left out `app.set` (all of `lib/application.js`) and the doc-comment examples. No code in `lib/` calls `res.header(...)` or `self.set`, and none calls it indirectly with `.call` or `.apply`. Every match is `this.set(...)` inside a `res.*` method, or `res.set(...)` in the router.

**`lib/response.js`**
- `res.links` (line 94): sets `Link`
- `res.send` (lines 175, 199, 206, 223): sets `Content-Type`, `Content-Length` and `ETag`
- `res.json` (line 276): sets `Content-Type`
- `res.jsonp` (lines 320, 321, 331, 332): sets `X-Content-Type-Options` and `Content-Type`
- `res.type` / `res.contentType` (line 625): one function, named `contentType`, and assigned to both properties
- `res.format` (line 699): the call is inside a callback; `format` is the outermost named method
- `res.attachment` (line 725): sets `Content-Disposition`
- `res.append` (line 756)
- `res.location` (line 924): sets `Location`
- `res.redirect` (line 982): sets `Content-Length`

**`lib/router/index.js`**
- `sendOptionsResponse` (line 654): `res.set('Allow', body)`

The calls at line 798 are `res.set` calling itself, so they're excluded.
